sampling_model.design: Observational independent sampling from one support-closed compact restricted additive-noise law \(P\).
sampling_model.units: The units \(V^{(1)},\ldots,V^{(n)}\) are independent draws of all \(d\) labelled nodes.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal target is the labelled DAG \(G_0\).
sampling_model.overlap: Innovation densities are strictly positive on relative interiors, conditional-support fibers are connected, feasible structural outputs stay inside the declared node intervals, and node variances are bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted local-polynomial regression estimates conditional means; held-out squared losses estimate risks, bounded continuous characteristic kernels estimate residual HSIC, and a separate residual-coordinate Lipschitz premise controls plug-in residual perturbations.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.3 assumes that any two orders with different ancestral-reversal counts are strictly fitness-ranked in the opposite direction and concludes that greedy search terminates at a true order.
The terminal-node normalized explained variance in a random linear causal chain converges to one under a positive mean log-edge-weight condition.
A causally minimal restricted additive-noise model satisfying the Condition 19 configuration requirement has a DAG identifiable from its observational distribution.
Greedy sparsest-permutation algorithms are pointwise consistent under faithfulness through weakly decreasing covered-arrow walks.
Sample splitting gives a fitted-residual dHSIC statistic the same asymptotic null distribution as its exact-residual counterpart.
Studentized cross-HSIC converges to a standard normal law under fixed bounded-kernel null distributions satisfying a second-moment condition.
A likelihood order estimator is consistent when the minimum wrong-order log-residual-variance gap is positive.

body.tldr: On support-closed compact restricted additive-noise models whose graph is a matching, the primitive edgewise inequality \(\rho^{\to}_{uv}>(d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\) forces every non-topological order to have a strictly improving reversal-correcting insertion. It follows directly that best-improvement GENE search and residual-independence pruning recover the labelled DAG with a finite oracle-query budget. A six-node smooth witness satisfies this local structural certificate while violating Li et al.'s global reversal-monotone premise through explicit score limits. Cross-fitted simultaneous risk and HSIC bands yield singleton recovery only when the primitive gain slack and a pruning separation margin dominate propagated uncertainty, and otherwise return a compatible graph set. A smooth open family with a trapped wrong order remains the first-class converse question.

project_justification.gap: Li et al. (2025, Theorem 4.3) impose a global score ranking over all pairs of orders with different ancestral-reversal counts. Peters et al. (2014) identify restricted ANMs through Condition 19 configurations, but this observational identification gives no local ascent property for GENE's hybrid score.
project_justification.niche: The missing theorem is a directly checkable condition on structural functions and noise laws that guarantees a correcting insertion, together with evidence that it covers identifiable laws excluded by global reversal monotonicity.
project_justification.fill: The pairwise forward-versus-reverse signal inequality yields a strict gain lower bound on support-closed matching-component ANMs. A six-node cosine--quadratic law proves strict separation from Li et al., and the resulting navigation theorem drives oracle recovery, query complexity, a calibrated positive witness, and margin-aware set-valued inference.

body.related_work: Li et al. (2025, Equation (6), Definition 4.1, and Theorem 4.3 with its proof on page 5) define the score and insertion search and assume global reversal monotonicity; Theorem 3 proves a strict reduction of that premise on a smooth six-node ANM. Peters et al. (2014, Condition 19, Definition 27, and Theorem 28 on pages 13--16) prove identification under their positive-density restricted-ANM configuration requirement. Their Proposition 17 supplies only the pointwise nonconstancy characterization of causal minimality; the positive-parent-law-measure formulation used here is a strengthened compact-support premise. They do not state the present compact-support, relative-interior version; Lemma 1 supplies support closure, connected conditional-support fibers, localization of the differential obstruction to a positive-density interior open set, and the null-boundary step. Reisach et al. (2023, Sections 3 and 5) show how normalized explained variance responds to mechanism and noise strength, informing the primitive ratios without supplying the GENE landscape theorem. Solus, Wang, and Uhler (2021, Proposition 8 and Theorem 9) analyze covered-arrow moves for a sparsity score, not insertion ascent for the GENE score. Pfister et al. (2018, Theorem E.2 and Proposition E.3) support bounded continuous characteristic kernels and fitted-residual sample splitting, but the residual-coordinate Lipschitz perturbation premise used for the \(a_n\) term in \(w_H\) is separate and explicitly nonstandard. Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas (2023, Theorems 6 and 7) derive cross-HSIC null limits but not adaptive GENE graph sets. Buhlmann, Peters, and Ernest (2014, Theorems 1 and 2) separate likelihood order estimation from pruning under a wrong-order variance gap, a different score and margin.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The structural certificate is sufficient and applies to matching-component DAGs; it does not characterize general GENE landscapes. Exact independence is discontinuous, so finite-sample singleton recovery is stated only on the separated HSIC parameter space and under a propagated score-radius inequality. The \(a_n\) residual-estimation contribution to the HSIC band uses an explicitly nonstandard residual-coordinate Lipschitz premise. The rare-component construction remains an open question until smoothing is shown to preserve both its strict risk inequality and nonzero reverse-residual HSIC.
body.honest_scope: The compact-support identification lemma, direct pairwise navigation theorem, six-node strict comparison, oracle recovery theorem, quadratic positive witness, and simultaneous-band theorem are proof targets. The structural result is sufficient on matching-component DAGs. The smooth trapped family is an open-ended construction problem. When \(d=2\), the navigation bound reduces to \(C_P((Y,X);2,1)\ge\rho^{\to}_{XY}-\rho^{\leftarrow}_{XY}/2>0\), the familiar forward-versus-reverse residual comparison for this exact score. The released Sachs workflow is only an audit case: a fixed chi-square threshold cannot certify a population margin, and intervention-informed reference orientations are not consequences of an observational acyclic ANM alone.
